# OpenTsiolkovsky

> Open-source rocket flight simulator (3DoF, multi-stage, launch to impact) by Interstellar Technologies. This web app runs the Rust simulation core compiled to WebAssembly entirely in the browser: 3D globe, charts, flight events, impact points of spent stages and jettisoned parts, and Monte Carlo impact dispersion.

## Opening a configuration by URL

The app reads its configuration from the URL fragment, which is never sent to the server:

- `#preset=<id>`: a bundled sample vehicle (MOMO, S-310, S-520, SS-520-5, Epsilon, H-IIA, H3, Saturn V, Ariane 5, ...).
- `#c=<payload>`: a configuration. The payload is JSON compressed with raw DEFLATE and encoded as base64url without padding. The JSON is one of:
  - the web app configuration (`ClientConfig`, as written by the app's share link and settings export);
  - a CLI parameter file (`param_*.json`, keys with units such as `"burn end time(time of each stage)[s]"`);
  - `{"legacy": <param_*.json>, "files": {"<csv file name>": "<csv text>"}}`: a parameter file with the CSV tables it references.

To build such links, use `openTsiolkovsky-cli share -c param.json` or the MCP tool `create_share_link`.

## Running simulations as an agent

The CLI and an MCP server (stdio) give machine-readable results: JSON Schema of the parameter file, validation, single runs, Monte Carlo dispersion and share links.

- [AI agents: JSON output, MCP server, share links](https://github.com/istellartech/OpenTsiolkovsky/blob/master/docs/ai.md)
- [Parameter file reference](https://github.com/istellartech/OpenTsiolkovsky/blob/master/docs/configuration.md)
- [Output files](https://github.com/istellartech/OpenTsiolkovsky/blob/master/docs/output.md)
- [Physics models and numerics](https://github.com/istellartech/OpenTsiolkovsky/blob/master/docs/physics.md)
- [Source code](https://github.com/istellartech/OpenTsiolkovsky)
